planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in rich, moist, well-drained acidic soil; this Exbury-strain Knap Hill hybrid was later used by Dr. Eugene Aromi as a parent of the Gulf Coast hybrid 'Red Pepper'.

directions: Gallipoli is a classic Knap Hill/Exbury deciduous azalea bearing slightly ruffled, crimson-red flowers set off by delicate brownish-green stamens against light green foliage. It forms a broad, upright, spreading shrub that typically reaches 4 to 10 feet tall and 4 to 6 feet wide, flowering in a showy late-spring display. Though best known today as the seed parent behind Dr. Eugene Aromi's Gulf Coast hybrid 'Red Pepper', it remains a worthwhile garden cultivar in its own right. Grow in rich, moist, well-drained, acidic soil in full sun to light shade, since it is somewhat drought-sensitive and benefits from a steady moisture supply.
sources: The Azalean (2003) — Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids chart

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; introduced in 1947, this Exbury/Knap Hill hybrid was later used by Dr. Eugene Aromi as a parent of the Gulf Coast hybrid 'Tensaw'.

directions: Oxydol is a 1947 Exbury/Knap Hill deciduous azalea prized for pure white, five-petaled, lightly scented flowers roughly 3 inches across, each marked with a narrow yellow blotch, opening wide on an upright, somewhat slender plant. Oval leaves emerge mid-green and turn rich red in autumn, giving the shrub two seasons of interest. It is exceptionally cold-hardy for a Knap Hill selection, tolerating winter lows near -34 degrees C, and was later crossed with Rhododendron austrinum by Dr. Eugene Aromi to produce the fragrant yellow-flowered 'Tensaw'. Grow in full sun to light shade in consistently moist, acidic, peaty, well-drained soil, since dry summer conditions can invite fungal leaf problems.
sources: The Azalean (2003) — Named Aromi Deciduous Hybrids chart

common_name: Golden Sunset Azalea (Exbury Deciduous Azalea, RHS AGM)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; bred by Lionel de Rothschild at Exbury and later used by Dr. Eugene Aromi as a parent of several Gulf Coast hybrids including 'Jane's Gold' and 'Canary Isles'.

directions: Golden Sunset is an Exbury-strain Knap Hill deciduous azalea bred by Lionel de Rothschild, carrying orange-red buds that open into large, light yellow flowers brushed with orange and lit by an orange flare in the throat. Trusses can hold up to 30 individual flowers nearly 2.5 inches across in a heavy late-May display, and the plant has earned the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for reliable garden performance. It grows into an upright shrub to roughly 5 feet tall and was later used by Dr. Eugene Aromi as a parent in several Gulf Coast hybrids, passing along its clear yellow coloring to selections like 'Jane's Gold'. Grow in full sun in consistently moist, acidic soil enriched with peat or sphagnum, since like other Knap Hill azaleas it resents drying out at the root.
sources: Millais Nurseries — Golden Sunset Deciduous Azalea AGM
